samples.summary: API-keys query failures are swallowed and rendered as "No API keys."
samples.evidence: `const { data: apiKeys = [] } = useQuery(...)` at workspace-settings.tsx:146 destructures only `data`; neither `isError` nor `error` is consulted anywhere in the section (lines 434-505). On any failure of `fetchApiKeys` (403 for a stale membership, 404 after the slug-rename invalidation described below, 5xx) the query resolves to the `[]` default and the UI positively asserts "No API keys." (line 503) with no toast and no error state — unlike the workspace query, which has an explicit `isError` branch at line 218. The new tests make this path reachable for every member, not just owners (`enabled: !!workspaceId` at line 149, where the invites query alongside it still carries `&& !!isOwner`), so a member whose listing fails is told they hold no keys and may mint duplicates rather than being told the fetch failed.

samples.summary: Unawaited clipboard write reports "API key copied" even when the copy failed, losing a show-once secret
samples.evidence: In the reveal dialog handler (lines 672-677) `navigator.clipboard.writeText(revealedKey.key)` is called without `await`/`.catch`, and `toast.success("API key copied")` fires unconditionally on the next line. `writeText` rejects in a non-secure context or when clipboard permission is denied; the rejection is unhandled and the user is told the copy succeeded. Because the dialog's own text says "Copy your key now. It will only be shown once" (line 660) and `setRevealedKey(null)` (line 683) discards the only in-memory copy, a false success means the secret is unrecoverable and the key must be re-minted. Same unguarded pattern as `copyInviteLink` (line 234), but there the token is re-readable from the list.

samples.summary: Member-side "no Created by column" assertion can pass vacuously before the `me` query resolves
samples.evidence: Line 253 waits only on `keyRow(MEMBER_KEY.name)`, which is gated on `fetchApiKeys` resolving, not on `fetchMe`. `isOwner` (workspace-settings.tsx:87) is `undefined` until the `me` query settles, so the negative assertions at lines 258-260 (`queryByRole("columnheader", { name: "Created by" })` is null) hold trivially in the unresolved state and prove nothing about the owner/member branch at line 460. The sibling test at lines 168-174 explicitly guards against exactly this by awaiting a control that depends on the auth query; the new API-key tests drop that discipline (lines 264-286 and 288-303 likewise exercise nothing identity-dependent despite their "non-owner member" titles).

samples.summary: Revoke API key button is not disabled while its mutation is pending, so a double click yields a spurious failure toast
samples.evidence: The button at lines 487-495 has no `disabled={revokeApiKeyMutation.isPending}`, unlike the create-key submit (line 639) and the create-invite button (line 371). The row stays in the DOM until the invalidated listing refetches, so two quick clicks fire `revokeApiKey` twice for the same id; the backend's `ApiKeyService.revoke` (api-key.service.ts:104) throws `NotFoundException` when `updateMany` matches zero rows, so the second call surfaces `toast.error("Failed to revoke API key")` (line 178) even though the revocation actually succeeded.
